what_happened: The operator wrote the request for job 20261023-165947-e7bd so that it told the producer to read another branch, archive/next4-2026-10-23. The producer works in a one-commit copy of the repo, and that copy does not contain the branch. The producer could not read the source, the job failed, and the operator carried the work by hand. The operator logged this as their own mistake.
cause: Admission and reading accept any ref, path or file name in a request as text, and nothing resolves it against what the producer will actually have. The producer's one-commit working copy is a hidden limit that neither the requester nor the reader is shown or checked against. The failure appears only at run time, as a producer that cannot read its source, with no diagnosis that points to the unreachable ref. The restore-from-archive case (jrc6) fails similarly, with no change and no diagnosis, so unreachable sources may be one hidden cause there.
prevention: Add a pre-dispatch check. It extracts every branch, ref and path the accepted reading names and tests each one against the producer's actual working copy, which is the one-commit checkout. If any is unreachable, the check refuses dispatch with a message that names the ref. It would also offer to stage the needed content into the working copy, for example as a pinned source snapshot or an exported file set. This is the same step that pins sources for study jobs. It would have refused the archive/next4-2026-10-23 request before the job ran.
proposed_request: Before a job is dispatched, make Athena check that every branch, ref, path or file named in the accepted reading can be read from the producer's one-commit working copy. If any cannot be read, refuse dispatch and name the unreachable item. Also support staging content from another branch, such as an archive branch, into the producer's input as a pinned source, so a request that needs it can run. Acceptance: (1) a request naming a ref that is absent from the working copy is refused before dispatch, with the ref named in the message; (2) a request that names an archive branch with staging gets its content in the working copy and the producer reads it; (3) a test covers both cases against a one-commit checkout.
